title: Snapshot update rule
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w$ be a binary input, and fix $t\in\mathbb N$ and a finite list of bits $l$. Suppose the first bit records whether $t=0$; when $t\ne0$, the second bit records whether the tableau had already accepted by time $t-1$. Suppose the remaining designated bits encode the input symbol and each work-tape symbol in the configuration at time $t$, by presence and value, and, when $t\ne0$, the snapshot field decodes to the machine's snapshot at time $t-1$. Then the snapshot update rule applied to $l$ yields the snapshot encoding at time $t$ followed by the acceptance indicator at time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: first bit equals the indicator of t=0
when t≠0, second bit equals the acceptance indicator at time t−1
input-symbol presence and value bits encode the time-t input symbol
for each work tape, presence and value bits encode its time-t symbol
when t≠0, decoded prior snapshot equals the run snapshot at time t−1
